description:
Milestone per ARCHITECTURE.md §12 v0.5.

Success criterion (quoted, per ARCH §12): Git tree view, live streaming, pulsing tool indicators, branch-state indicators. Tailing the event log is the only read mechanism. (The 'tailing' phrasing is being retired by bl-bcd9 — the real mechanism is filesystem watching. Restated below.)

=== Restated success criterion (post bl-bcd9) ===

An egui/eframe-based frontend that, against a live conversation repo:
- Renders a git tree view of conversations (root and subagent), tool calls, and merges.
- Shows live streaming text for in-flight model calls.
- Shows pulsing indicators for in-flight tool calls.
- Shows branch-state indicators (in-flight, merged, stopped, conflicted).
- Issues user actions (new prompt, stop, resume) exclusively via 'lernie <subcommand>' invocations.
- Holds no persistent state: every render is a pure function of filesystem state at the current git ref.

=== Stack ===

egui/eframe (pure Rust programming model; winit-based windowing with no webview dep). Chosen once implementation started: Dioxus-desktop required libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev on Linux, a heavy version-specific system dep incompatible with the repo's 'no weird system libs' aesthetic. egui's only runtime deps are the X11/Wayland libs already present on any Linux desktop session. The pluggability contract (§3.5) is unchanged; a future browser-based 'lernie-ui-web' crate would share the pure-Rust view-model layer.

=== Contract (pinned by bl-bcd9) ===

Frontend reads and watches paths under the conversation repo. Frontend writes nothing to the repo. Frontend→harness commands go exclusively through 'lernie <subcommand>' invocations. Multiple frontends may run concurrently against one repo. See §3 / §7 of ARCHITECTURE.md for the enumerated surface once bl-bcd9 lands.

=== Layout dependency ===

This epic assumes the v0.3 conversation-repo layout pinned by bl-7c23 (commit abfe713). The frontend's watched paths target the new shape: steps/<conv-id>/<NNN>/, sibling subagent worktrees with hyphenated descent names, summary/<NNN>.md, etc. No .agent/, no exchanges/, no inv/.

=== Hard dependencies (do these first) ===

- bl-bcd9 — ARCH doc revision. Blocks anything that depends on the frontend/backend contract being pinned down.
- bl-7c23 — v0.3 layout migration. Without it the on-disk shape the frontend reads doesn't exist yet.
- bl-4772 (v0.2 git tree) — needed for branch-state indicators and no-ff merge topology rendering. Without it, only v0.1's flat 'commit on main' shape exists.
- bl-683c (v0.3 tools epic) — needed for pulsing tool-call indicators and tool output rendering.
- v0.4 epic (subagent dispatch, not yet filed) — needed for sub-branch arrows to live subagents and the nested-tree view.

User's standing direction: if this epic has dependencies, note them, and the earlier epics get done first. So this epic is filed as a roadmap anchor; actual claim happens once bl-bcd9 + bl-7c23 + bl-4772 are merged.

=== Parallel-ok work that could start before deps ship ===

If we want to move sooner, the following subtasks do NOT depend on v0.2+ and could be claimed once bl-bcd9 merges:
- egui skeleton: Cargo wiring, basic window, no-op render.
- Filesystem watcher: inotify + polling fallback (ARCH §3.1), isolated module with its own tests.
- CLI outbound wrapper: thin Rust abstraction that exec's 'lernie <subcommand>' and streams stdout/stderr back; reusable by any future frontend.
- Git tree renderer against v0.1-shape repos: renders the flat 'one commit per conversation step on main' shape that v0.1 already produces. Extends naturally when v0.2 adds branches.

These can be filed as subtasks under this epic once bl-bcd9 is merged; leaving them latent until then.

=== Out of scope ===

- History-view forking from old commits (v1, not v0.5 — flagged in ARCH §7.2).
- Workflow-config UI (v0.6).
- Task-suite UI (v0.7).
- Replay/tarball UI (v0.8).
- Embedding in another tool — that's the standing 'exec lernie' pattern, no UI work required.

=== Testing strategy ===

Per AGENTS.md: 'if it can't be tested, it mustn't be built.' The stateless-frontend discipline makes most of this testable without pixels:
- Renderer functions take (filesystem snapshot) -> (view model). Unit-test against real fixtures (small, hand-constructed lernie repos on disk — not mocks).
- Filesystem watcher tested against real tmpfs events.
- CLI outbound tested against a fake 'lernie' binary on PATH (shell stub), no mocking of the Rust call site.
- View-model-level tests for the widget logic (pure functions over fixture repos — the view-model layer has no egui dep). Pixel-level smoke tests gated behind a feature flag so CI can run them only in environments with a windowing server available.

100% coverage per repo precommit hooks.

=== Done-when ===

End-to-end demo: open a fresh conversation repo, run 'lernie prompt <repo> "hello"' in one terminal, and the live frontend renders the conversation branch spawning, the streaming response, the merge back to main, with branch-state indicators flipping through in-flight → merged. Kill the process mid-stream and see the stopped marker.

All subtask gates closed. cargo test + tarpaulin --fail-under 100 green on merge.
